definitions.explanation: Pork meat that has been finely chopped or passed through a grinder. One of the most commonly used ground meats in Japanese and East Asian cooking.

examples.japanese: {豚|ぶた}ひき{肉|にく}で{餃子|ぎょうざ}を{作|つく}る。
examples.english: To make gyoza with ground pork.

examples.japanese: {豚|ぶた}ひき{肉|にく}を{二百|にひゃく}グラムください。
examples.english: I'd like 200 grams of ground pork, please.

examples.japanese: {麻婆豆腐|まーぼーどうふ}には{豚|ぶた}ひき{肉|にく}を{使|つか}うのが{定番|ていばん}だ。
examples.english: It's standard to use ground pork for mapo tofu.

notes:
A compound of {豚|ぶた} (pork), ひき (ground/minced, from {挽|ひ}く 'to grind'), and {肉|にく} (meat). The most versatile ground meat in Japanese home cooking.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {豚|ぶた}ひき{肉|にく}の{炒|いた}め{物|もの}: stir-fried ground pork
- {豚|ぶた}ひき{肉|にく}の{肉|にく}みそ: meat miso (ground pork cooked in miso)
- {豚|ぶた}ひき{肉|にく}の{餡|あん}: ground pork filling
- {豚|ぶた}ひき{肉|にく}を{炒|いた}める: to stir-fry ground pork

RELATED WORDS:
- {鶏|とり}ひき{肉|にく}: ground chicken — leaner alternative
- {牛|ぎゅう}ひき{肉|にく}: ground beef — used for Western-style dishes
- {合|あい}いびき{肉|にく}: ground meat blend (usually pork and beef) — popular for ハンバーグ (hamburger steaks)
- ひき{肉|にく}: ground meat — the general term

USAGE:
{豚|ぶた}ひき{肉|にく} is the go-to ground meat for Chinese-Japanese dishes like {麻婆豆腐|まーぼーどうふ}, {担々麺|たんたんめん}, {餃子|ぎょうざ}, and {春巻|はるま}き (spring rolls). It is also essential for {肉味噌|にくみそ}, a versatile condiment used as a topping for {冷|ひ}やし{中華|ちゅうか} and rice.
